concerns.question: The supplied facts cannot distinguish the broader, case-specific meaning of being run as a business from the parenthetical income test. Both formulas rely on the expressly retained operational abstraction.
The supplied Boolean facts can express the rival negation attachments, but cannot determine which grammatical interpretation is intended.

The supplied facts do not encode occupation, continuity, capability of profit, or the qualified force of “should not in the ordinary course”. Those considerations remain outside the antecedent predicate and cannot be inferred from its truth value.

The surrounding regulated-activity, carve-out and territorial conditions cannot be evaluated using these three facts. Neither formula determines a licensing trigger, exemption, compliance status or entitlement.
The regulatory-intent sentence does not supply a separate Boolean condition or remove the qualified wording of the preceding conclusion.
Does the preceding “not” govern both coordinated business indicators, or does “or” join independently sufficient negative descriptions?
Does “in the ordinary course” qualify only the licensing-perspective conclusion rather than the disputed antecedent?

The supplied income fact cannot distinguish the parenthetical income test from the broader case-specific assessment of being run as a business. Occupation or duty, continuity, and capability of profit are not represented. A reading treating the parenthetical as illustrative rather than exhaustive would therefore require null formalization under this vocabulary; it cannot be implemented by silently redefining the supplied fact.

The Boolean fragment does not express the qualified force of should not in the ordinary course or regulatory intent. These remain qualifications on the conclusion, not additional encoded antecedent conditions.
The genuine-family fact combines genuineness, single-family status, and investment-serving purpose. It cannot separately test those descriptions or determine family membership.
